_meta.purpose: Inference rules for classifying captured symmetric keys when the API symbol alone is ambiguous (e.g., BCryptGenerateSymmetricKey hits without an immediate algorithm tag). Used by sym_key_inference.py to fill in the 'algorithm' field of key_inventory entries that the upstream pipeline left as '?'. Each rule carries a spec citation per repo rule (no entry without a spec citation).
_meta.decision_order: rules are evaluated in order; the first match wins.

rules.name: tdes_24
rules.spec_citation: NIST SP 800-67 Rev 2 §3.1 (Triple DES, three-key option, 168 bits). WITHDRAWN 2024-01-01 (NIST SP 800-67r2). TDEA is no longer an NIST-approved block cipher; rule retained for historical corpus only.
rules.note: citation section corrected from §3 to §3.1; WITHDRAWN status (2024-01-01) added; historical_only flag set so downstream consumers do not treat this as a current-recommendation inference.

infer.note: Likely the HMAC-internal zero-padded ipad/opad key buffer residue (RFC 2104) — externally-supplied keys of exactly 64 bytes are uncommon; context priority: hmac|kdf preferred to disambiguate from ed25519_extended_secret_64.

rules.name: hkdf_extract_prk
rules.spec_citation: RFC 5869 §2.2 (HKDF-Extract — output length = HashLen = 32 bytes for SHA-256)

rules.name: rc4_variable
rules.spec_citation: Schneier 1996 §17.1 (Applied Cryptography 2nd ed) + Microsoft CNG RC4 deprecation notice 2008
rules.note: RC4 supports variable key length 5-256 bytes. Cerber early variants (2016) used RC4. Modern Windows deprecated.

rules.name: tea_xtea_xxtea_16_byte
rules.spec_citation: Wheeler & Needham, FSE 1994 §3 (TEA — 128-bit key, 32-round) + Needham & Wheeler 1997 (XTEA) + 1998 (XXTEA)
rules.note: HDLocker uses TEA-16 variant for ransom-note key encoding (paper §IV-B).

rules.name: aes_rcon_table_40

infer.algorithm: AES Rcon table (10 words × 4 bytes per FIPS-197 §5.2 Figure 11)

rules.spec_citation: FIPS-197 §5.2 Figure 11 (Rcon[i] is a 4-byte word [x^(i-1),00,00,00]; AES-128 KeyExpansion uses 10 Rcon words = 10 × 4 = 40 bytes, NOT 10 bytes).
rules.note: previous rule used key_len_bytes=10 with confidence 0.8 — directly contradicts FIPS-197 which defines Rcon[i] as a 4-byte word, not a single byte. Length-only inference of a 10-byte buffer as Rcon table is unsupported by the spec. Rule renamed aes_rcon_table_10 -> aes_rcon_table_40, key_len_bytes corrected to 40, confidence demoted to 0.5, and a byte_match_any pattern gate is required so the Rcon bytes (01 02 04 08 10 20 40 80 1b 36) actually match — preventing 10-byte / 40-byte length-only false positives. Flag as auxiliary, not a real cipher key.

rules.name: chacha20_nonce_12
rules.note: 12-byte residue near a ChaCha20 sink is the per-message nonce, not the key.  Flag as auxiliary.

rules.name: des_56_or_3des
rules.spec_citation: FIPS 46-3 §7.1 (DES 56-bit key, padded to 64 bits with parity)
rules.note: 8-byte keys are rare in modern ransomware (DES is broken). Some legacy variants (early 2000s) still observed; tag as 'DES (legacy)' with low confidence.

rules.name: aes_128_key_len
rules.note: 16-byte key MAY also be Camellia-128 / SEED / ARIA-128 but those are extremely rare in modern ransomware corpus (none observed in our 165-sample set). AES-128 is the dominant 16-byte key cipher.

rules.name: aes_256_default_32_byte
rules.note: removed 'WannaCry' example -- WannaCry is AES-128 (16-byte key) per Secureworks analysis (https://www.secureworks.com/research/wcry-ransomware-analysis); it must match aes_128_key_len, NOT this rule. Representative 32-byte examples: Crysis/Phobos, Ako, GandCrab v1-v3. A raw key||nonce blob captured at a wrap input is excluded: the trailing bytes are a stream-cipher nonce, not a 128-bit block IV, so the 32-byte length does not imply AES there.

rules.name: ed25519_extended_secret_64

infer.algorithm: Ed25519 extended secret key (32B private scalar + 32B prefix)

rules.spec_citation: RFC 8032 §5.1.5 (Ed25519 expansion: H(k) = scalar||prefix, 64 bytes total)
rules.note: 64-byte residue often appears in modern RaaS that uses Curve25519 / Ed25519 (Embargo, Conti, LockBit 3.0).  Same length collides with HMAC-SHA-512 block-padded key — disambiguate via context.
